description: A transplant medical director must assign one deceased-donor kidney between two listed recipients and finalize the immediate transplant plan, with input from transplant nephrology, immunology, social work, and the operating-room coordinator.

shared_context.S1: One deceased-donor kidney is available for immediate allocation, and two listed recipients, Recipient A and Recipient B, are being considered.
shared_context.S2: The transplant medical director makes the binding allocation decision and records the immediate operative plan.
shared_context.S3: The hospital's allocation policy gives priority to a compatible recipient who qualifies for the highly sensitized candidate exception.
shared_context.S4: The transplant team must complete allocation and operative planning during the current coordination huddle before the organ is released to another center.
shared_context.S5: As part of the transplant service's routine huddle, Dr. Mehta checks with nephrology, immunology, social work, and the operating-room coordinator before finalizing the allocation.

PF1.text: Recipient A has a calculated panel-reactive antibody level of 98% and qualifies for the hospital's highly sensitized candidate exception; Recipient B does not qualify. Dr. Alvarez confirmed the listing data this morning, but the exception flag has not yet been entered in the allocation note.

PF2.text: The final virtual crossmatch is negative for Recipient A and positive for Recipient B, so the kidney is immunologically compatible with Recipient A but not Recipient B. Nina released these results to the transplant laboratory queue ten minutes ago.

PF3.text: Recipient A's named caregiver has signed a commitment to provide continuous home support for the first 14 days after discharge, including transportation to every required follow-up visit. Marcus received the signed form today, but it is not yet attached to the transplant chart.

PF4.text: The transplant operating room is available for Recipient A at exactly 6:30 AM, and the donor kidney must be implanted no later than 9:00 AM to meet the accepted preservation plan. Elise has reserved the room verbally, but the start time is not yet in the operative schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The kidney must be assigned to Recipient A because Recipient A is the compatible highly sensitized candidate.
The settlement must record that Recipient A's crossmatch is negative.
The operative start time must be exactly 6:30 AM.
The care plan must document 14 days of continuous caregiver support.
An operating-room reservation commitment for Recipient A must be recorded.
The highly sensitized exception must be cited as a justification for the allocation.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'operating_room_reservation' and c['target'] == 'Recipient A' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Recipient A's exact 98% sensitization level qualifies A, but not B, for the policy exception that determines which compatible recipient receives the kidney and supplies the required allocation justification.
The negative crossmatch for Recipient A and positive crossmatch for Recipient B establish that A is the compatible recipient and require the settlement to record A's exact negative status.
The signed caregiver commitment specifies exactly 14 days of continuous support, changing the discharge plan from an unspecified support arrangement to a documented 14-day requirement.
The reserved operating-room window fixes Recipient A's start at exactly 6:30 AM and requires an explicit operating-room reservation commitment rather than an unscheduled transplant plan.
